docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• BindPlane account and project
  • Dynatrace tenant
  • Dynatrace token with the following permissions:
    • logs.ingest
    • metrics.ingest
  • One of:
    • For working entirely in a browser: access to GitHub Codespaces
    • For working locally in a Dev Container:
      • VSCode
      • Dev Containers Extension installed
      • Docker (more about this in the next section)
  • Yes! let's begin

docs.title: 1. Bindplane
docs.text: Begin by creating a Bindplane account, then create a project to work in.

docs.title: 2. Dynatrace
docs.text:
In your Dynatrace tenant, create a platform token that has the following permissions:

  • logs.ingest
  • metrics.ingest

Save the token for now; you won't be able to see it again once you leave the token creation dialog.

docs.title: 3. Development Environment
docs.text:
The lab work will be done inside a Dev Container - a fully configured development environment that is bootstrapped with all of the dependencies required for the lab.

You have two options to work with the Dev Container:

docs.title: A. GitHub Codespace
docs.text:
This is the lowest-friction way to get up and running. You can simply launch a browser-based session of VSCode without having to install anything locally

Codespaces Quota

GitHub Codespaces are a billed resource, however GitHub provides a free monthly quota. If you would rather not incur any charges against your quota for this lab, use option #2

  1. Visit this repository's page in GitHub
  2. Expand the "<> Code" menu
  3. Click "Create codespace on main"

docs.title: B. Local Dev Container
docs.text:
Working with a local Dev Container involves an integration with your IDE. Visual Studio Code (VSCode) is well-suited for this This overall process is described in the Visual Studio Code documentation.

In summary:

  1. Install Docker.
  2. Install VSCode.
  3. Install the official Dev Containers extension.
  4. Clone this repo and open it up in VSCode
  5. Use the VSCode Command Palette to Select "Dev Containers: Reopen in Container"

docs.title: Validate the Environment
docs.text:
We'll be doing all of our work inside this Dev Container. Take a look at the terminal tab at the bottom of of your VSCode window. You should see some messages confirming that the environment has started up correctly.

Press any key or open a new terminal window to continue.

This host writes its logs to files in /var/log/bpsystem. Navigate to that directory and view the contents

> cd /var/log/bpsystem
> ls
auth.log  cron.log  kern.log  syslog

Let's take a look at the logs being written to syslog by tailing the syslog file 

> tail -f syslog

Your logs may look slightly different based on some environmental factors like hostname or docker implementation.

Great! With that, your environment is set up and ready to go!

  • Let's install our Bindplane Agent

docs.title: Let's get started on installing our Bindplane Agent
1. Navigate to your Bindplane account
docs.text: Click the button "Install Agent"

docs.title: 2. Specify your agent confguration
docs.text:
You can use the default, stable Agent Type.

You can leave "Fleet" blank.

Choose Linux for the platform and click "Next"

docs.title: Install the agent
docs.text:
You'll be shown a command that installs the agent. Copy it and run it in your terminal.

You should see some text scroll by, and a message indicating that the Bindplane agent was installed.

You may see some messages instructing you to use systemctl to start the Bindplane service. DON'T DO THAT! In this environment, you have a command called startBindplane instead. Go ahead and run that in your terminal.

> startBindplane

Bindplane Startup

Don't use the systemctl command to start Bindplane as the installation script mentions. Instead, use the startBindplane command.

Once you've run that command, you should see your agent show up in the Bindplane UI. It will be named after the host it is installed on. If you are using a Codespace, it will be your Codespace name. If you are using a local Dev Container, it will take the name of your Docker implementation.

Go ahead and click "Create a Configuration" and we'll start ingesting some logs!
